'''Shulamit Levenberg''' (born 1969 in [[Israel]]) is an Israeli [[professor]] of [[Biomedical engineering|Biomedical Engineering]] at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion - Israel Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=פרופ' שולמית לבנברג |url=https://bme.technion.ac.il/team/%D7%A4%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%A4-%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%9E%D7%99%D7%AA-%D7%9C%D7%91%D7%A0%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%92/}}</ref> She is the head of the Stem Cell and Tissue Engineering Laboratory and served as the Dean of the Faculty of Biomedical Engineering from 2016 to 2020.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Levenberg Lab – Stem Cell and Tissue Engineering Laboratory |url=https://levenberglab.net.technion.ac.il/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=levenberglab.net.technion.ac.il}}</ref> Her research focuses on [[tissue engineering]] from [[stem cell]]s, [[Vascularisation|vascularization]] of engineered tissues, and cell [[Cellular differentiation|differentiation]] on polymeric scaffolds.<ref name=":1" />

== Biography and academic career ==
Levenberg attended the Ulpanat Kfar Pines high school and completed her national service as a [[tour guide]] at a field school in Jerusalem.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2010-08-04 |title=סיפור הצלחה: 20 הנשים המשפיעות בישראל |url=https://www.news1.co.il/Archive/0024-D-50679-00.html |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=www.news1.co.il |language=he}}</ref> She earned her Bachelor of Science ([[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]]) in [[Biology]] from the Faculty of Medicine at [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem|the Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Shulamit Levenberg |url=https://iias.huji.ac.il/people/shulamit-levenberg |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=iias.huji.ac.il}}</ref> She then completed a direct [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] track in [[Molecular Cell Biology]] at the Feinberg Graduate School of the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] under the supervision of Professor Benjamin Geiger.<ref name=":3" />

Following her doctorate, she conducted her post-doctoral research at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT).<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Meet 3 Trailblazing Women - Shulamit Levenberg |url=https://www.bsf.org.il/magazine/winter-edition-2020/meet-3-trailblazing-women-shulamit-levenberg/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=BSF |language=en-US}}</ref> She worked at MIT for five years as a research associate in the lab of Professor Robert Langer.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Shulamit Levenberg |url=https://ats.org/about/faces-of-the-technion/shulamit-levenberg/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=American Technion Society |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2011–2012, she spent a sabbatical year as a visiting professor at [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":3" />

== Research and scientific work ==
Levenberg conducts interdisciplinary research focused on [[stem cell]]s and [[tissue engineering]].<ref name=":3" /> She is the head of the Stem Cell and Tissue Engineering Laboratory and also serves as the director of the Technion Center for [[3D bioprinting|3D Bioprinting]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> Her pioneering work focuses on the in vitro [[Vascularisation|vascularization]] of [[Tissue engineering|engineered tissues]] to improve the survival and perfusion of engineered grafts upon implantation.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5" /> Her laboratory was the first to engineer vascularized tissue flaps, offering novel reconstruction techniques using engineered tissue constructs.<ref name=":3" /> Additionally, her research investigates the effects of scaffold stiffness and mechanical tensile forces on the early [[Cellular differentiation|differentiation]] and 3D organization of stem cells on [[Biodegradable polymer|biodegradable polymeric scaffolds]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> She has also developed unique stem-cell engineered tissue constructs aimed at inducing the regeneration and repair of injured [[spinal cord]]s.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /> Levenberg's lab utilizes these complex tissue models to deepen the understanding of various disease mechanisms and to improve tissue repair applications, including bone and muscle reconstruction.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7" />

== Entrepreneurship and commercial ventures ==
In addition to her academic research, Levenberg is a prominent figure in the [[biotechnology]] and [[food technology]] sectors, translating laboratory innovations into commercial applications.<ref name=":6" /> In 2017, she co-founded [[Aleph Farms]], a [[cellular agriculture]] company, alongside the food-tech incubator "The Kitchen Hub" of [[Strauss Group]] and entrepreneur Didier Toubia.<ref name=":6" /> Serving as the company's Chief Scientific Advisor, she leveraged her extensive expertise in 3D bioprinting and tissue engineering to help develop the world's first slaughter-free [[Cultured meat|cultivated steak]] grown on a plant protein matrix.<ref name=":6" /> Beyond her work in [[cellular agriculture]], Levenberg has expanded her entrepreneurial ventures into the medical and diagnostics fields.<ref name=":8" /> She is the Co-founder and Scientific Advisory Board member of NurExone Biologics, which focuses on translational applications for [[Spinal cord injury|spinal cord regeneration]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":8" /> Additionally, she co-founded NanoSynex, a medical technology company utilizing a [[Microfluidics|microfluidic]] nanoliter droplet platform developed in her lab for rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":1" />

== Awards and recognition ==
Levenberg has received numerous prestigious national and international awards for her scientific contributions.<ref name=":0" /> In 2006, she was named a "Research Leader" in tissue engineering by Scientific American as part of their Top 50 scientists list.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=אשכנזי |first=שני |date=2021-03-01 |title=50 הנשים המשפיעות של ישראל 2021: פרופ' שולמית לבנברג |url=https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001362316 |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=גלובס |language=he}}</ref>

In 2018, she received the Rappaport Prize for Biomedical Research in the Senior Researcher category.<ref>{{Cite web |title=about |url=https://www.rappaport-prize.org.il/en/shulamit-levenberg |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250622210120/https://www.rappaport-prize.org.il/en/shulamit-levenberg |archive-date=2025-06-22 |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=www.rappaport-prize.org.il |language=en}}</ref> She was awarded the Bruno Memorial Award in 2019.<ref name=":3" />

In 2022, she was featured in Forbes magazine's "50 Over 50" list for [[Europe]], the [[Middle East]], and [[Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-07 |title=50 Over 50: EMEA 2022 |url=https://www.forbesafrica.com/woman/2022/02/07/50-over-50-emea-2022 |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=www.forbesafrica.com |language=en}}</ref> Most recently, in 2023, she was elected as a Fellow of the American National Academy of Inventors (NAI).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Shulamit Levenberg |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/shulamitlevenberg/}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Levenberg is married to Yehuda, and they have six [[child]]ren.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=מעמיקים אל שורשי המחלות |url=https://kolhamada.isf.org.il/article/%D7%9E%D7%A2%D7%9E%D7%99%D7%A7%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%90%D7%9C-%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%A9%D7%99-%D7%94%D7%9E%D7%97%D7%9C%D7%95%D7%AA/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=kolhamada.isf.org.il |language=en-US}}</ref> They live in [[Moreshet]], a communal settlement in the [[Misgav Regional Council]] in the [[Lower Galilee|Lower Galilee region]] of [[Israel]].<ref name=":2" />
